notes.whyTheseNumbersChanged: v1's five numbers were round aspirations (250 KB / 416 KB / 300 KB / 1150 KB) written as a gate and never run: no CI job executed check-bundle.mjs, and measured against HEAD on 2026-08-23 THREE of the five failed — entry 287,644 > 256,000, initial 482,196 > 425,984, total 1,273,275 > 1,177,600. A budget nobody ran is not a budget. v2 replaces the wishes with a RATCHET: each ceiling is the measured value of a green build plus a stated margin, so a regression is caught on the day it lands instead of being invisible behind a number that was already red. The aspiration is not thrown away — it is kept below, as `target`, which is where it belonged all along.
notes.margin: ~5% over measured, on every byte ceiling. Wide enough that ordinary feature work does not churn this file; far tighter than the 76,736-byte regression that returning the dev MockCore to the entry chunk would cause, which the v1 ceilings would have accepted in silence.
notes.measuredOn: 2026-08-23, production `vite build`, after ADR-130 (the dev MockCore left the production entry and the first-paint surfaces came back into it).

target.owed: Total JS is 32,746 bytes over the standing aspiration and cannot be closed by splitting: `vendor-support` (256,274 bytes) is lodash + ajv + d3, pulled in transitively by @jsonforms and @xyflow, and NONE of it is on the startup path. Closing it means changing one of those two dependencies, which is a decision, not a chore. notes.whyTheseNumbersChangedAgain: 2026-08-26: the entry ceiling was RE-BASELINED 174,000 -> 199,000, and the reason is written down because `notes.margin` says a ceiling raised without knowing which change spent the bytes is not a ceiling. It was red on HEAD before this session touched anything, and BISECTED rather than guessed: eleven commits built from clean detached checkouts, entry chunk measured by `stat` each time — 86df2ea 166,665 / ff5b73a 167,559 / e5f74ff 167,552 / 1ec9478 167,526 / b610775 167,535 / f5b5d19 168,044 / 6932aab 168,044 / 096be3a 168,044 / 4e845c5 168,769 / b2cd35e 168,769 / 58e181c 188,679. One commit, +19,910 bytes, straight through a 174,000 ceiling. `58e181c` landed `theme/icons.tsx` (878 lines, 161 inline-SVG drawings — 166 path literals costing 7,575 bytes in the entry alone), `theme/assets.tsx` and `theme/timeline.tsx` as NEW files; `icons.tsx` and `assets.tsx` are reachable from first paint because the Engines rail, the header, the hierarchy and the empty state all draw marks before anything else loads. That is `first-paint.json`'s counter-rule exactly: a surface whose job is to be there when you first look cannot be the one that loads last, and an icon that pops in after the chunk arrives is the ADR-131 blank-control defect arriving late instead of never. So the bytes are DELIBERATE and the stale number is the defect. The new ceiling is a measured green build (189,845, this tree, after ADR-147 moved the settings-sheet family out of the entry) plus the same ~5% margin. ADR-147's own contribution is 1,166 bytes of that, measured against 58e181c's 188,679. The INITIAL ceiling moves with it and for the same reason, not as a second judgement: initial = the entry plus the two chunks it statically imports (vendor-react, vendor-state), so every byte of the entry is also an initial byte. HEAD measured 383,231 against 378,000 — red on its own, before this session — and this tree measures 384,397. Both new ceilings are a measured green build plus ~5%. The other three were and remain green at both points: largest 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,267,741 <= 1,272,000, 33 chunks >= 24.

notes.whyTheInitialChanged: 2026-09-01 (ADR-197): the INITIAL ceiling was re-baselined 403,000 -> 425,000, and the reason it had to move is a DEFECT IN THIS FILE rather than a feature. Every entry byte is also an initial byte and the two vendor chunks the entry statically imports are a constant 194,552 (vendor-react 193,968 + vendor-state 584), so `maximumInitialJavaScriptBytes` states a second, implied ceiling on the ENTRY: 403,000 - 194,552 = 208,448. `whyTheEntryChangedAgain` below raised the entry ceiling to 210,000 and left this number alone — correctly observing that initial still fit AT THAT MOMENT (395,119) and not noticing that the pair now disagreed by 1,552 bytes. Every build in that band is GREEN on the entry gate and RED on the initial one, and that is what shipped: 139b065 measures entry 209,845 (155 bytes under its own ceiling) and initial 404,397 (1,397 over this one), so `check-bundle.mjs` — which CI runs — has been failing on a build that passes every ceiling anyone was watching. Measured as an exact A/B in this worktree, two production `vite build`s minutes apart: with this run's only front-end change (the ADR-197 warning block in RenderDialog) reverted, entry 209,845 and initial 404,397 — BYTE-IDENTICAL, because that block lands in the lazy CutscenePanel chunk (total 1,329,496 -> 1,329,828, +332). So none of the overage is this pass's. The +9,278 entry bytes since `whyTheEntryChangedAgain`'s 200,567 are the sixteen commits that touched editor/src between f6bb8ca and 139b065 — the cinematics arc (ADR-173/175/177/182/190/192/193/195) and the UI lane's shell vocabulary (ADR-189) — every one of which was measured against the entry ceiling raised for exactly that growth, and none against this one. New ceiling = the measured build (404,397) plus the same ~5% margin every other ceiling here carries, which also clears the implied-entry arithmetic (210,000 + 194,552 = 404,552). AND THE PAIR IS NOW INTERLOCKED: `check-bundle.mjs` fails if an entry at its own ceiling would not fit under the initial one, so raising one without the other is a gate failure with the arithmetic in the message rather than a trap armed for the next lane. THE OTHER FOUR DO NOT MOVE, which is the check on this one: entry 209,845 <= 210,000, largest 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,329,828 <= 1,351,000, 35 chunks >= 24.
notes.whyTheEntryChangedAThirdTime: 2026-09-01 (ADR-201): the ENTRY ceiling was RE-BASELINED 210,000 -> 220,000, and the number that justifies it is the one measuring HEAD rather than this tree: 2eebc77 builds an entry of 209,998 bytes, which clears the ceiling it was given by TWO BYTES. That is not a budget with margin in it, it is a budget that fails on the next edit to any entry-reachable file whatever that edit is, and this pass is simply the edit that arrived first. Measured as an exact A/B in this worktree, three production `vite build`s minutes apart against one `node_modules`, reverting this run's front-end sources to HEAD as BYTES: all three reverted 209,998; `session.ts` alone restored 210,061; all three restored 210,074. So the walk costs 76 bytes of entry, of which 13 are `session.ts` (the `progress` argument on two signatures, and the five fields the browser stub's refusal now carries) and the remainder is the module graph around a lazy chunk that grew — `CutscenePanel` itself is 39,420 bytes in its OWN chunk and none of it is startup work. The bytes are deliberate and the two-byte headroom is the defect. New ceiling = this measured green build (210,074) plus the same ~5% margin every other ceiling here carries. THE OTHER FOUR DO NOT MOVE, which is the check on this one: initial 404,626 <= 425,000, largest 256,274 <= 270,000, total 1,334,527 <= 1,351,000, 35 chunks >= 24. AND THE INTERLOCK STILL HOLDS WITHOUT MOVING THE INITIAL CEILING: an entry at 220,000 plus the 194,552 bytes of vendor chunks it statically imports is 414,552, which is 10,448 under 425,000 — so the pair the ADR-197 note found disagreeing stays consistent, and `check-bundle.mjs` proves it rather than this sentence.
